label: t1-reporter-data
topic: Track 1 data and reproducibility: Cello UCF libraries for threshold-steepness separability
summary: Downloaded three Cello UCF libraries (Eco1C1G1T1 4,834,067 B; Eco2C1G5T1 46,518 B; SC1C1G1T1 1,744,232 B; git blob SHA-1 of each matches GitHub's tree listing) and ran analyse.py and refit.py. All design-reporter pair numbers reproduced exactly (BM3R1 dn 0.1587, S 12.01; 6 pairs with Kfold>=2; phage 933W dn 0.2124 S 6.74; yeast LexA dn 0.2604 S 4.68; SrpR S1 terminator differs; yeast CI/CI434 cassettes identical). One count differs: the design says 9 strict calibration pairs but its own list, and the data, give 10. A first run of the P3 cytometry refit (not previously reported) gives Pearson r = 0.972 between refit and shipped n, max refit dn 0.1115, and finds 10 of 20 gates with small non-monotone upticks at the highest input levels, which the design's day-2 exclusion rule would have dropped. Holdout libraries Eco1C2G2T2, Eco2C1G3T1 and Bth1C1G1T1 were deliberately NOT downloaded by me; only sizes and blob SHAs from the GitHub tree are recorded.
lay_summary: Synthetic biologists build tiny genetic switches that turn a gene off when another is on, like a dimmer that goes from bright to dark as you turn a knob. Two numbers describe each dimmer: where the knob must sit for the light to halve, and how sharply it flips. An earlier team claimed you can change the first number a lot without changing the second, by tweaking only one DNA 'volume dial' on the switch. I downloaded the public tables of measured switches and re-ran the sums. Every pair-by-pair number the earlier team quoted came out the same, except they counted nine matching pairs where there are really ten. I also re-estimated the sharpness myself from the raw cell measurements, and it agreed closely with the published values.

glossary.plain: A smooth S-shaped curve that describes how an output falls (or rises) as an input grows.
The input level at which the output is half way between its high and low values.
How abruptly the curve flips; bigger n is a sharper switch.
A short DNA stretch that sets how strongly a gene is turned into protein.
A JSON file that lists the parts and measured switch curves of a Cello library.
A genetic switch where one protein shuts off a gene's output.
A fingerprint of a file; any change to the file changes it.
A number from -1 to 1 saying how closely two lists of numbers rise and fall together.
Relative difference in steepness between two gates: |n1-n2| divided by their average.
How many times bigger the larger threshold is than the smaller.
The separability index log2(Kfold)/dn: octaves of threshold shift per unit of steepness drift.
Data kept unseen until the test is frozen so it cannot be tuned to.

could_not_find: Did not download holdouts Eco1C2G2T2, Eco2C1G3T1, Bth1C1G1T1 on purpose (pre-registration). Files for the first two already exist under data/t1-deep (seen in a directory listing, not opened) and the scout's scratch holds Eco1C2G2T2, so the 'untouched' status in the design is already compromised and should be disclosed.
Earlier scout and laws numbers were not individually re-checked beyond what design-reporter restates; law set 1.8.1 was not used here.
No bootstrap CIs for refit n. Histogram 'output' values assumed to be counts per bin.
python -I blocks site-packages here, so the refit needs -P and numpy/scipy.
Cause of the design's '9 pairs' count not known (likely miscount).
recommendations: Fix the strict-pair count to 10 in PREREG.
Replace the exclude-non-monotone-gates rule with a tolerance before freezing.
Disclose that holdout files were already opened by the scout and possibly t1-deep.
Add bootstrap CIs; run the refit on holdouts only after the freeze.
